definitions.title: Restoration Time (boundary-parameterized)
definitions.absenceIsNotImplementationProof: Other adopted source statements and code branches may supply the mathematical contract; see full sourceFields

sourceFields.Standard reference: EKAS-defined; bare "MTTR" is not a valid name — see family note
sourceFields.Required parameter: Declared boundary, selected from named semantic anchors: t0 required-function-lost, t1 failure detected/alarmed, t2 maintenance notified, t3 request acknowledged/technician dispatched, t4 technician at asset, t5 diagnosis/active work begins, t6 physical repair complete, t7 test/restart complete (technically available), t8 operations/quality releases asset, t9 stable required rate and quality achieved. Not every source provides every anchor
sourceFields.Formula (per declared boundary): `Technical restoration = t7 − t0 or t7 − t1` (start basis named); `Production recovery = t8 − t0`; `Restart and release delay = t8 − t7`
sourceFields.Grain: Failure event; a mean of monthly/asset/departmental means is invalid
sourceFields.Eligibility: Eligible when start and end anchors for the declared boundary are present, semantically validated, and produce a non-contradictory sequence. Contradictory sequences are quarantined and reported, not silently dropped. Open events are reported with count and age, never excluded silently
sourceFields.Reference value / source precedence: Where several sources can supply an anchor, precedence is declared per anchor and recorded per event. Equipment-state anchors take precedence over administrative anchors for restoration boundaries; a control-system run signal alone is not proof of restoration
sourceFields.Configure down: Administrative timestamps only → publish MET-023 instead, statement: "restoration time not computed, administrative proxy only." No response anchor → statement: "response decomposition unavailable" (total restoration elapsed remains available where supported). No reason-coded transitions → statement: "delay decomposition unavailable," EKAS will not allocate unobserved elapsed time to a cause. Technical restoration only → statement: "production recovery unverified." No qualifying events → statement: "no qualifying repair events occurred in the selected period" — this is not a restoration time of zero
sourceFields.Coverage: Every result reports eligible-against-candidate event count, coverage percentage, excluded count with reasons, open-event count, source systems, semantic validation status. Distribution (median, an upper percentile, maximum, event count) is reported alongside the mean; a mean without distribution is not published
sourceFields.Prohibited: Work-order lifecycle timestamps are not relabelled as restoration time; earliest-to-latest labour punch is not treated as active repair; overlapping states are not added; repair/replacement/reset/bypass/no-fault-found events are not pooled without stratification. A high restoration time does not support a claim that repair execution is slow, nor a recommendation for additional preventive maintenance without failure-mode, recurrence, condition, or causal evidence. A falling restoration time is not reported as improvement without checking repeat-failure behaviour, repair-action type, and first-time fix
sourceFields.Certification state: Eligible for current-state certification once gates pass, at its declared boundary and decomposition; results at different boundaries are reported separately or normalised to a common validated boundary before aggregation
sourceFields.Oracle: Per D.11 (clean event per boundary; concurrent technicians; pause/resume; technical-restoration-vs-production-recovery divergence; 1-failure/2-WO and 2-failure/1-WO; contradictory-sequence quarantine; open-at-period-end; mixed-boundary non-aggregation)

definitions.title: Production Commitment Exposure
definitions.sourceFormulaField: Per eligible commitment line: `open_quantity = committed_quantity − accepted_shipped_quantity − approved_finished_goods_allocation`. `confirmed_exposure = true` when at least one governed deterministic condition applies: approved scheduled completion is after the required ship-ready cutoff; an unresolved quality hold prevents fulfilment; a required routing operation is blocked with no approved alternate/recovery plan; a production stop has invalidated the approved completion plan; required material, tooling, or qualified capacity is unavailable within the current plan. `gross_exposed_quantity = SUM(open_quantity where confirmed_exposure)` within compatible units of measure only
definitions.absenceIsNotImplementationProof: Other adopted source statements and code branches may supply the mathematical contract; see full sourceFields

sourceFields.Standard reference: EKAS-defined; new certified headline metric with its own reference answer
sourceFields.Claim: That the current approved plan no longer satisfies a customer commitment unless something changes — a **current state claim**, not a forecast
sourceFields.Measures inside the result contract: Exposed Commitment Count; Gross Open Quantity On Exposed Commitments
sourceFields.Formula: Per eligible commitment line: `open_quantity = committed_quantity − accepted_shipped_quantity − approved_finished_goods_allocation`. `confirmed_exposure = true` when at least one governed deterministic condition applies: approved scheduled completion is after the required ship-ready cutoff; an unresolved quality hold prevents fulfilment; a required routing operation is blocked with no approved alternate/recovery plan; a production stop has invalidated the approved completion plan; required material, tooling, or qualified capacity is unavailable within the current plan. `gross_exposed_quantity = SUM(open_quantity where confirmed_exposure)` within compatible units of measure only
sourceFields.Commitment states: ON_PLAN and CONFIRMED_EXPOSURE are current-state claims; PROJECTED_AT_RISK is a governed scenario output, not this metric; COMMITMENT_MISSED is a historical fact; STATUS_UNKNOWN is a refusal
sourceFields.Grain: Customer order line, resolved through production order, routing operation, and current schedule state; the site-level result aggregates independently verified line-level outcomes. Quantities aggregate only within compatible units of measure
sourceFields.Required inputs: Customer commitment quantity, required ship-ready/delivery cutoff, current approved schedule version, scheduled completion time, actual accepted completion quantity, production-order-to-customer-order linkage, routing/operation status, current hard-block status, approved alternate/recovery status
sourceFields.Reference value / source precedence: Where an APS/ERP/MES owns the approved planned completion, EKAS consumes and certifies that source fact; EKAS does not become a scheduling engine
sourceFields.Eligibility: A commitment line is eligible when linkable to production with a resolvable routing state and an effective cutoff. Unlinkable lines count as unknown, never as not-exposed; unknown commitment count is a required output field
sourceFields.Configure down: No authoritative scheduled completion → may state commitments are linked to active production disruptions, may not state confirmed exposure — statement: "customer commitment exposure cannot be verified. The current approved completion schedule is unavailable." No order-to-production linkage → the metric is not published, claim reduces to production-plan status
sourceFields.Coverage: Required output: eligible commitment count, covered commitment count, unknown commitment count, coverage percentage, source freshness, exclusion reasons
sourceFields.Prohibited: `gross_exposed_quantity` does not mean units will be late, permanently lost, must be additionally produced, are recoverable, or are the predicted shortfall — it means remaining units whose current approved fulfilment path requires intervention. Work in progress is not counted as completed finished product; quality-held units are not counted as available; customer due date is not substituted for the ship-ready cutoff; missing orders are not treated as not exposed; an active disruption is not linked to every order on a machine, only the affected routing window. The presentation layer does not compute this result from certified components; the language model does not derive it by reasoning over several metrics — it is produced by the governed calculation authority and rendered, never derived at presentation time
sourceFields.Certification state: Eligible for current-state certification once gates pass. Projected shortfall and recoverable-units-before-cutoff are governed scenario outputs, never displayed under the same certification treatment as this result
sourceFields.Result contract minimum fields: metric identifier and version, as-of timestamp, horizon start/end, ship-ready cutoff basis, site scope, commitment grain, exposure rule version, exposed commitment count, gross exposed quantity by unit of measure, unknown commitment count, eligible/covered commitment count, coverage percentage, schedule version, source freshness, lineage references, exclusion reasons, oracle version, certification status
sourceFields.Oracle: A designed commitment ledger, independently calculated, frozen and content-hashed separately from any dataset generator, at customer-order-line grain, covering: full/partial completion; split orders and combined production jobs; finished-goods allocation; partial shipments; quality hold/release; rework/scrap; cross-midnight cutoffs; schedule revisions; alternate qualified assets; multiple routing operations; missing links; duplicate joins; stale source timestamps; incompatible units; one unknown order line in an otherwise complete population. Owned by WP-P4-18 (commitment exposure oracle)

definitions.title: Quoted-versus-Demonstrated Rate Gap
definitions.absenceIsNotImplementationProof: Other adopted source statements and code branches may supply the mathematical contract; see full sourceFields

sourceFields.Canonical name / aliases: **Quoted-versus-Demonstrated Rate Gap**. Aliases: quoted-rate gap, demonstrated-rate gap, rate leakage. The alias “margin leakage” is an operational shorthand only; it does not assert a margin-dollar value.
sourceFields.Claim being measured: Whether the observed good-production rate for an eligible job is below the governed quoted/standard rate that priced that job, at the declared part × operation × asset grain. This is a rate-variance observation, not an adjudication or correction of any customer record.
sourceFields.Formula / state logic: For eligible run population *i*: `demonstrated_rate_i = good_parts_i / qualified_machine_production_time_i`; `rate_gap_i = quoted_rate_i − demonstrated_rate_i`; `rate_gap_percent_i = rate_gap_i / quoted_rate_i`. A positive rate gap means the demonstrated rate is below the quote. `quoted_rate_i` must be greater than zero and use the same unit basis and effective configuration as the demonstrated rate. `rate_gap_percent` is not calculated when the quote is absent, zero, incompatible, or the run population is insufficient.
sourceFields.Grain and aggregation: Native result grain is job × part × operation × asset × quoted-rate revision × closed observation window. Demonstrated rate aggregates only as `Σ good_parts / Σ qualified_machine_production_time` over compatible native records; simple averages of job, asset, or rate-gap percentages are invalid. A package result contains its eligible component-job results and a package severity roll-up; it does not invent a single rate or rate-gap percentage across unlike parts, units, operations, assets, or quoted-rate revisions.
sourceFields.Scope and time basis: Uses closed machine-production intervals and accepted good-part counts attributed to the job, part, operation, and asset. The time window, source watermark, quoted-rate effective date/revision, and package membership revision are mandatory output fields. Labour-reported hours are not a permissible time basis.
sourceFields.Required / optional inputs: Required: job identity and package membership where applicable; part, operation, asset, and unit basis; accepted good-part counts; qualified machine-production time; governed customer-asserted quoted/standard rate with effective date/revision; and the run-population qualification record. Optional: customer-supplied cost-severity configuration and its effective revision; explanatory reason classifications; and a package decision label.
sourceFields.Reference values and source precedence: The quoted/standard rate is customer-asserted governed configuration, not calculated, normalized, overridden, or “corrected” by EKAS. The governed configuration record for the job/part/operation/asset and effective time takes precedence. Demonstrated rate uses count-based good-production signals and qualified machine time; labour clocking, generic `throughput_by_part`, nominal/rated speed, and an estimator's recollection are not substitutes.
sourceFields.Eligibility and exclusion: A result is eligible only when all required identifiers join unambiguously, the count and machine-time population is qualified, the quoted-rate record is effective and unit-compatible, and the default qualification rule is **300 consecutive parts within a 1–8-hour production window, unless a customer-approved governed override is effective**. Trials, engineering/test production, rework re-entries, unassigned counts/time, and intervals outside the declared job boundary are excluded and reported. The default follows the AIAG PPAP Manual Significant Production Run definition; Ford/GM Run at Rate (`GM1927-35`) is corroborating capacity-verification precedent, not an alternate metric formula.
sourceFields.Configure-down / refusal behavior: If the population does not meet the governed default or an effective customer-approved override, publish `INSUFFICIENT_RUNS` with candidate and qualified run counts, not a numeric gap. Missing or incompatible quoted rate yields `QUOTED_RATE_UNAVAILABLE`; missing qualified machine time or accepted-good counts yields `DEMONSTRATED_RATE_UNAVAILABLE`; ambiguous job/package linkage yields `SCOPE_UNRESOLVED`. None is coerced to zero or replaced by a generic throughput measure.
sourceFields.Coverage and quality treatment: Every result reports candidate, qualified, included, excluded, and insufficient-run counts; coverage percentage; exclusions with reasons; count/time completeness; lineage; source freshness; and semantic-validation status. Package status preserves component-level coverage and never lets a fully covered component conceal an unknown or insufficient component.
sourceFields.Oracle / reference-answer requirements: This derived metric requires its own independently calculated, frozen, content-hashed oracle and acceptance corpus; certification is not inherited from its inputs. The oracle must cover: below/equal/above quoted rate; rate-unit incompatibility; zero or missing quote; count/time mismatch; labour-hours substitution rejection; insufficient runs; mixed assets and quoted-rate revisions; package with unlike parts; partial package coverage; effective-date change; and severity states unavailable, below fully absorbed cost, and contribution-negative.
sourceFields.Prohibited substitutions and claims: EKAS must not derive the quote, replace machine time with labour hours, use `throughput_by_part`, average component rates, treat missing data as zero, write back to customer systems, claim a lost dollar value, claim causation, or state that a job is “unprofitable” from the rate gap alone. A rate gap is not a capacity, OEE, scheduling, ERP, or pricing correction.
sourceFields.Output / certification state: Numeric output: quoted rate, demonstrated rate, absolute gap, percentage gap, unit basis, and result evidence profile. Severity output is independently nullable: `CONTRIBUTION_NEGATIVE`, `BELOW_FULLY_ABSORBED_COST`, `NOT_BELOW_FULLY_ABSORBED_COST`, or `SEVERITY_UNAVAILABLE`. `CONTRIBUTION_NEGATIVE` and `BELOW_FULLY_ABSORBED_COST` are distinct customer-configured classifications; neither is inferred from rate variance or converted into dollars. A numeric result is certifiable only after the MET-028 oracle, lineage, coverage, and acceptance gates pass.
sourceFields.Evidence-surface requirements: Per job: canonical ID/version, grain, window, quote revision, source lineage, eligibility/refusal state, coverage and quality profile, numeric fields when eligible, and severity state with configuration revision when available. Per package: membership revision, all component results and refusal states, compatible-unit groups, coverage summary, and the highest observed severity without suppressing component evidence. Generic hypothetical examples may use Part X and Machine Y only.
sourceFields.Versioning and recertification triggers: Any change to formula, qualifying-machine-time definition, accepted-good-count treatment, grain, aggregation, quote precedence, eligibility, the 300-part/1–8-hour threshold or override rule, severity-state semantics, package roll-up, or oracle requires a new definition version and recertification. Changes to a customer quoted-rate or severity configuration revision change the affected result lineage and require recomputation, not a definition rewrite.
sourceFields.Open decisions: `[TBC-417: governed customer configuration contract and data mapping for quoted rate and distinct cost-severity classifications]`. This gap blocks the affected claim rather than authorizing a default.

definitions.title: Dollar Valuation Layer
definitions.absenceIsNotImplementationProof: Other adopted source statements and code branches may supply the mathematical contract; see full sourceFields

sourceFields.Canonical name / aliases: **Dollar Valuation Layer**. Aliases: standard-cost conversion variance; dollar-impact layer.
sourceFields.Claim being measured: The governed standard-cost conversion variance for eligible reconciled conversion hours under the visible active valuation lens. It is a decision-support exposure, not proof of realized cash effect, contribution margin, profitability, quote correction, or price correction.
sourceFields.Formula / state logic: Under the first governed lens, `dollar_impact = reconciled_conversion_hours × standard_shop_rate` at the declared compatible scope and basis. The output requires a current approved `standard_shop_rate` and the reconciled hours result. Presence states remain explicit: `EXPLICIT_VALUE` and `EXPLICIT_ZERO` are numeric; `NOT_MODELED` and `UNKNOWN_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` are nonnumeric and never coerced to zero. The dollar figure is not governed as a binary show-or-suppress outcome: it carries a visible confidence band. `HIGH` requires rate and allowances explicit, approved, and current; `MEDIUM` permits current-standard substitutes for unavailable quote values or an estimated not-modeled allowance; `LOW` signals significant reliance on unknown or default inputs. Exact band thresholds and computation method are `[TBC-420]`; no numeric threshold is implied here.
sourceFields.Grain and aggregation: Native result grain is the compatible reconciled job × part × operation × asset × quote/configuration revision × closed observation window. Aggregate only by summing eligible native dollar-impact components with the same active valuation lens and compatible standard-shop-rate basis; never average dollar figures, rates, confidence bands, or incompatible components.
sourceFields.Scope and time basis: Uses the closed reconciliation window and the approved rate effective for that result scope. The output retains the reconciled-hours window, active valuation lens, rate version, allowance/configuration versions, and source watermark.
sourceFields.Required / optional inputs: Required: eligible reconciled conversion hours; active lens identifier; QAC-001 `standard_shop_rate` record with value, unit/basis, presence state, approval, effective date, and version; and required allowance presence states. Optional: approved explanatory reason classifications and the Package/Commercial decision label.
sourceFields.Reference values and source precedence: The first and only governed lens is standard-cost conversion variance, using the QAC-001 `standard_shop_rate` record. An effective, approved, scope-matched record takes precedence; an explicit governed current-standard substitute is allowed only when recorded as such. No other valuation lens is configured by this ruling.
sourceFields.Eligibility and exclusion: Eligible only when the hours result is reconciled at the declared scope, the rate record is unambiguous, applicable, approved, current, and basis-compatible, and all required lineage is retained. Exclude unresolved scope, incompatible bases, stale or unapproved rate records, unreconciled hours, and any input that cannot be attributed to the declared result.
sourceFields.Configure-down behavior: If the first lens or required rate cannot support a numeric result, publish the governed refusal state and affected presence states; do not substitute a generic rate or claim a dollar value. If a numeric result is supported, show the confidence band adjacent to it; reduced confidence limits the claim but is not itself a suppression rule.
sourceFields.Coverage / quality treatment: Report included and excluded components, input-presence states, reconciliation state, rate approval/currentness, configuration versions, coverage, quality, lineage, and confidence band. Unknown/default reliance must be visible in the band and supporting evidence.
sourceFields.Oracle / reference-answer requirements: A separate, independently calculated, frozen, content-hashed oracle and acceptance corpus are required. They must cover explicit value, explicit zero, not-modeled, source-unavailable, approved current-standard substitute, incompatible basis, stale/unapproved rate, unreconciled hours, mixed compatible/incompatible aggregation, each visible confidence state, and refusal behavior. Certification is not inherited from MET-028, QAC-001, or the hours result.
sourceFields.Prohibited substitutions / claims: Do not use labour hours, nominal rates, unapproved defaults, blended rates, missing-as-zero treatment, an undisclosed valuation lens, or an invisible confidence label. Do not claim incremental cash effect, contribution-margin exposure, full profitability, realized savings, bid correctness, price correctness, causation, or a recommendation to change price.
sourceFields.Output / certification state: Output includes dollar-impact value when eligible, currency/unit basis, active valuation lens, visible `HIGH`/`MEDIUM`/`LOW` confidence band, reconciled-hours reference, rate and allowance/configuration versions, and evidence profile. The metric is uncertified until its own oracle, lineage, coverage, acceptance, and certification gates pass. CR-051 admits MET-029 to Phase 4 certification scope; it does not certify it.
sourceFields.Evidence-surface requirements: At the same glance, render the dollar-impact figure as primary and its confidence band adjacent; render the active valuation lens visibly; render the existing governed hours figure directly beneath as secondary and unchanged under its existing reconciliation-or-suppress rule. Full methodology, evidence drawer, quote source, and time bridge remain one interaction deeper. The Package/Commercial surface must provide an estimator enough decision cover to act without presenting an aggressive price as proven.
sourceFields.Versioning / recertification triggers: Any change to formula, active-lens semantics, rate/allowance presence-state meaning, source precedence, rate approval/currentness rule, grain, aggregation, eligibility, confidence-band method or thresholds, evidence surface, oracle, or prohibited claim requires a new definition version and recertification.
sourceFields.Open decisions: `[TBC-420: exact HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW thresholds and whether confidence is computed per figure or per presence-state combination]`. Future valuation-lens configuration beyond standard-cost conversion variance, visual styling beyond the governed hierarchy, and connections to broader learning or autonomous capabilities are out of scope.
